Classification-Based Decoding¶

API Details¶

a module for classification-based neural decoding

neurora.decoding.bidirectional_transfer_decoding(data1, labels1, data2, labels2, n=2, navg=5, time_opt='average', time_win=5, time_step=5, n_iter=10, normalization=False, pca=False, pca_components=0.95, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky', random_state=None)¶

Conduct bidirectional transfer decoding for EEG-like data.

Parameters:

  • data1 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials1, n_chls, n_ts1]) – Data from condition 1.

  • labels1 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials1]) – Labels for condition 1.

  • data2 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials2, n_chls, n_ts2]) – Data from condition 2.

  • labels2 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials2]) – Labels for condition 2.

  • n (int, default=2) – Number of categories for classification.

  • navg (int, default=5) – Number of trials averaged into each pseudo-trial.

  • time_opt ({"average", "features"}, default="average") – Strategy for handling time points within each time window.

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Size of the time window in samples.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows in samples.

  • n_iter (int, default=10) – Number of repeated random pseudo-trial averaging iterations.

  • normalization (bool, default=False) – Whether to standardize features.

  • pca (bool, default=False) – Whether to apply PCA.

  • pca_components (int or float, default=0.95) – Number of PCA components, or explained variance ratio.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across subjects using joblib.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

  • random_state (int or None, default=None) – Random seed.

Returns:

  • con1_to_con2_accuracies (ndarray, shape [n_subs, n_train_windows1, n_test_windows2]) – Transfer decoding accuracies from condition 1 to condition 2.

  • con2_to_con1_accuracies (ndarray, shape [n_subs, n_train_windows2, n_test_windows1]) – Transfer decoding accuracies from condition 2 to condition 1.

neurora.decoding.ct_decoding_kfold(data, labels, n=2, navg=5, time_opt='average', time_win=5, time_step=5, nfolds=5, nrepeats=2, normalization=False, pca=False, pca_components=0.95, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky', random_state=None)¶

Conduct cross-temporal decoding for EEG-like data using cross-validation.

Parameters:

  • data (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials, n_chls, n_ts]) – EEG-like neural data.

  • labels (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials]) – Trial labels for each subject.

  • n (int, default=2) – Number of categories for classification.

  • navg (int, default=5) – Number of trials averaged into each pseudo-trial.

  • time_opt ({"average", "features"}, default="average") – Strategy for handling time points within each time window.

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Size of the time window in samples.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows in samples.

  • nfolds (int, default=5) – Number of cross-validation folds.

  • nrepeats (int, default=2) – Number of repeated random pseudo-trial averaging iterations.

  • normalization (bool, default=False) – Whether to standardize features using the training data.

  • pca (bool, default=False) – Whether to apply PCA after optional normalization.

  • pca_components (int or float, default=0.95) – Number of PCA components, or explained variance ratio.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across subjects using joblib.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True. If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

  • random_state (int or None, default=None) – Random seed for reproducible pseudo-trial averaging and cross-validation.

Returns:

accuracies – Cross-temporal decoding accuracies.

The second dimension is training time, and the third dimension is testing time.

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_subs, n_windows, n_windows]

neurora.decoding.tbyt_decoding_kfold(data, labels, n=2, navg=5, time_opt='average', time_win=5, time_step=5, nfolds=5, nrepeats=2, normalization=False, pca=False, pca_components=0.95, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky', random_state=None)¶

Conduct time-by-time decoding for EEG-like data using cross-validation.

Parameters:

  • data (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials, n_chls, n_ts]) – EEG-like neural data.

  • labels (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials]) – Trial labels for each subject.

  • n (int, default=2) – Number of categories for classification.

  • navg (int, default=5) – Number of trials averaged into each pseudo-trial.

  • time_opt ({"average", "features"}, default="average") –

    Strategy for handling time points within each time window.

    • ”average”: average time points within each window.

    • ”features”: use all time points within each window as features.

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Size of the time window in samples.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows in samples.

  • nfolds (int, default=5) – Number of cross-validation folds.

  • nrepeats (int, default=2) – Number of repeated random pseudo-trial averaging iterations.

  • normalization (bool, default=False) – Whether to standardize features using the training data.

  • pca (bool, default=False) – Whether to apply PCA after optional normalization.

  • pca_components (int or float, default=0.95) – Number of PCA components, or explained variance ratio.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across subjects using joblib.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True. If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

  • random_state (int or None, default=None) – Random seed for reproducible pseudo-trial averaging and cross-validation.

Returns:

accuracies – Time-by-time decoding accuracies.

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_subs, n_windows]

neurora.decoding.unidirectional_transfer_decoding(data1, labels1, data2, labels2, n=2, navg=5, time_opt='average', time_win=5, time_step=5, n_iter=10, normalization=False, pca=False, pca_components=0.95, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky', random_state=None)¶

Conduct unidirectional transfer decoding for EEG-like data.

The classifier is trained on data1 and tested on data2.

Parameters:

  • data1 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials1, n_chls, n_ts1]) – Training-condition EEG-like data.

  • labels1 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials1]) – Labels for data1.

  • data2 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials2, n_chls, n_ts2]) – Testing-condition EEG-like data.

  • labels2 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_trials2]) – Labels for data2.

  • n (int, default=2) – Number of categories for classification.

  • navg (int, default=5) – Number of trials averaged into each pseudo-trial.

  • time_opt ({"average", "features"}, default="average") – Strategy for handling time points within each time window.

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Size of the time window in samples.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows in samples.

  • n_iter (int, default=10) – Number of repeated random pseudo-trial averaging iterations.

  • normalization (bool, default=False) – Whether to standardize features using data1.

  • pca (bool, default=False) – Whether to apply PCA after optional normalization.

  • pca_components (int or float, default=0.95) – Number of PCA components, or explained variance ratio.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across subjects using joblib.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True. If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

  • random_state (int or None, default=None) – Random seed for reproducible pseudo-trial averaging.

Returns:

accuracies – Unidirectional transfer decoding accuracies.

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_subs, n_train_windows, n_test_windows]
